research_question: Can Q.ANT's native Fourier/KAN-style layer preserve useful Fashion-MNIST classification accuracy with a competitive parameter budget compared with conventional ReLU networks, when the architecture is fixed before evaluation?
observations: Exp009 showed that parameter-efficient dense ReLU architectures transfer from MNIST to Fashion-MNIST, but it did not test a Q.ANT-specific nonlinear architecture.
The official Q.ANT toolkit defines calc_kan_layer_fprop as a sum of trainable amplitudes times a cosine-related periodic optical nonlinearity over input channels and fixed frequency components.
The official Q.ANT example QFourier layer trains amplitude and phase parameters in PyTorch using cosine and uses calc_kan_layer_fprop for evaluation.
Q.ANT publicly positions native nonlinear operations and KAN-style/Fourier networks as a key architectural use case for its photonic processor.
hypothesis: A Q.ANT QFourier classifier using the toolkit's native KAN-style periodic layer can reach the Fashion-MNIST accuracy-versus-parameter Pareto frontier against selected ReLU controls under the same training/test split and seed protocol.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if every tested QFourier configuration is dominated by at least one ReLU control on both mean Q.ANT-backend accuracy and trainable parameter count, or if Q.ANT-versus-PyTorch inference disagreement is large enough to invalidate the comparison.

proposed_method.training_reference: Train QFourier amplitude/phase parameters with the exact cosine formulation used by Q.ANT's official QFourier example; evaluate the trained QFourier candidates through qant.ai.calc_kan_layer_fprop on the Q.ANT CPU backend.

limitations: This experiment evaluates the Q.ANT CPU backend, not real photonic hardware performance.
The CPU backend's periodic function is an approximation of the hardware-related tcos behavior, so PyTorch cosine and Q.ANT outputs must be compared explicitly.
Fashion-MNIST remains a small grayscale benchmark and three seeds limit precision.
A favorable parameter trade-off would support further study of Q.ANT-native architectures, not prove latency or energy advantages.
